affordance_in_statement: An expected position is specified by a non-zero integer $l$. The absolute value $|l|$ identifies the switch index ($1 \le |l| \le n$). The sign of $l$ defines a target state $t(l)$, where $t(l) = 1$ if $l > 0$, and $t(l) = 0$ if $l < 0$. A relay will trip and shut down the system if and only if both of its monitored expected positions are simultaneously violated... As long as at least one of the two expected positions is actually held... the relay remains stable.
removal_suggestion: Present the switch relations through a physical or network process (e.g., directed signals, dependencies, or forbidden pair states) rather than standard signed CNF literals with 'at least one satisfied' disjunction.
